hero.blurb: Crawls a library's docs, embeds them on your machine, and serves hybrid search to you and to Copilot.

demo.question: how do I proxy API requests to my backend

arch.alt: Architecture: VS Code commands and the Copilot language-model tool call into extension.ts, which runs a discovery, scrape, chunk, embed pipeline and a hybrid search engine; data lives in the docs site, a local MiniLM model and a sql.js SQLite file in VS Code global storage.
arch.title: How the pieces fit.
arch.footnote: Nothing leaves the machine except page fetches and the one-time model download.

flow.alt: Indexing flow: discover pages from sitemap.xml or by crawling, scrape main content, split into ~512-token chunks, embed each with MiniLM, store in SQLite, then search with keyword and vector ranking fused by RRF.
flow.kicker: INDEX ONE LIBRARY, END TO END
flow.title: From a URL to answers.
steps: sitemap.xml first, else crawl 3 levels deep
main/article text, nav and footer removed

decisions.alt: Design decisions: sql.js instead of native SQLite, local Transformers.js embeddings, reciprocal rank fusion, sitemap-first discovery.
decisions.title: Why it's built this way.
items: SQLite compiled to WASM (storageEngine.ts:28) needs no native rebuild per Electron version. The whole DB is in memory and written to disk with db.export().
Transformers.js runs all-MiniLM-L6-v2 in the extension host (embeddingsEngine.ts:26): no API key, no doc text sent to a provider.
Keyword and vector scores aren't comparable, so ranks are fused instead: 1/(60+rank) summed per chunk (searchEngine.ts:121).
One sitemap.xml fetch beats a 3-level crawl; URLs are kept only if they start with the configured URL (discoveryEngine.ts:49).

stack.alt: Stack: TypeScript, VS Code Extension API, webpack; Transformers.js with all-MiniLM-L6-v2; cheerio and node-fetch; sql.js SQLite.
stack.title: The stack.

terminal.alt: Terminal: npm ci, then npm run compile builds dist/extension.js with webpack and copies sql-wasm.wasm; then press F5 in VS Code to launch the Extension Development Host.
terminal.title: Up and running.

editor.alt: Code from src/search/searchEngine.ts lines 121 to 147: reciprocal rank fusion. Each keyword and vector result adds 1/(60+rank+1) to its chunk's score, so chunks found by both rise to the top.
editor.title: Hybrid search in a few lines.
